title: Revelation 10 — The mighty angel with the little book + the seven thunders

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT), ed. Michael W. Holmes (Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software, 2010), printed text with the variant-marker sigla removed. Primary uncial witnesses for Revelation: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01) and Codex Alexandrinus (A/02), with Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04) and P47/P115 where extant; Codex Vaticanus (B/03) does not contain Revelation in its original hand. Variants against NA28 and the Byzantine/Textus Receptus tradition are reported in the verse commentary (overlay convention sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation).

verdicts.reasoning: allon angelon ischyron katabainonta ... peribeblēmenon nephelēn, kai hē iris epi tēn kephalēn autou, ... hoi podes autou hōs styloi pyros. Exact; the pillar-of-fire entry correctly left as background for a simile.
echōn en tē cheiri autou biblaridion ēneōgmenon; ethēken ton poda autou ton dexion epi tēs thalassēs. 'little book, opened' exact.
ekraxen phōnē megalē hōsper leōn mykatai; elalēsan hai hepta brontai tas heautōn phōnas. Exact.

citations: SBLGNT (no variant marker in 10:4: the Byzantine majority text also lacks the additions)
verdicts.reasoning: hote elalēsan hai hepta brontai, ēmellon graphein ... Sphragison ha elalēsan ... kai mē auta grapsēs. Exact. TR additions tas phōnas heautōn and moi correctly attributed to the TR only (the SBLGNT apparatus shows Robinson-Pierpont agrees with SBLGNT here). Reception note (no God; men like himself) verified and confined to the note; the line keeps 'Seal up'.
ho angelos, hon eidon hestōta epi tēs thalassēs kai epi tēs gēs, ēren tēn cheira autou tēn dexian eis ton ouranon. Exact; Dan 12:7 noted.
hoti chronos ouketi estai 'that there will be delay no longer' (ASV, RSV, NRSV) against KJV 'time no longer': context (vv 6-7) and BDAG support 'delay'. Disputed against KJV; defensible.

all' en tais hēmerais ... kai etelesthē to mystērion tou theou, hōs euēngelisen tous heautou doulous tous prophētas. Proleptic aorist with kai-apodosis rendered 'then the mystery of God is finished' (ASV). 'servants' per overlay. Reception note verified; the line renders to mystērion tou theou literally. No leakage.
hē phōnē hēn ēkousa ... palin lalousan ... kai legousan: anacoluthon resolved with a finite verb, noted. Exact in sense.
apēltha pros ton angelon legōn autō dounai moi to biblaridion; Labe kai kataphage auto, kai pikranei sou tēn koilian. 'stomach' for koilia defensible; historic present 'he says' kept.
elabon ... katephagon auto, kai ēn en tō stomati mou hōs meli glyky ... epikranthē hē koilia mou. Exact.
legousin moi (indefinite plural); Dei se palin prophēteusai epi laois kai ethnesin kai glōssais kai basileusin pollois. 'over' (ASV) keeps the range of epi + dative; noted.

citations: SBLGNT (Holmes 2010) variant markers at Rev 16:18 and 21:3, and their absence at 8:7, 10:4, 12:17, 16:7, 21:2
Metzger, A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament (2nd ed. 1994)
glossaryReview.reasoning: claim_type direct is right: the entry declares which text is translated and how variants are reported. Three accuracy fixes. (1) The 8:7 omission is a Textus Receptus (minority) reading, not that of the Byzantine majority text, which the SBLGNT apparatus shows agreeing with SBLGNT; rephrase wherever 'Byzantine' is said there. (2) Add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou, quoted by the canon's English) to the wohChoice list of KJV-wording variants, and 16:18 (NA28 singular anthrōpos egeneto; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'). (3) Add REV-WOH-16:18's NA28 divergence to the 'NA28 bracketed or divergent readings reported' sentence. The decision itself stands.

citations: LXX usage: kyrios for the Tetragrammaton, theos for ʾĕlōhîm
glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct: theos never renders the Tetragrammaton in the LXX or NT, the canon's French reads 'Dieu' at every site, and published chapters 1, 4, 6 use 'God'. The canon's English 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' is recorded in reception notes without entering the line.

Direct is defensible: both senses are lexical and the context split (divine master vs free/slave pair) is the ASV/RSV/NRSV practice and the 1:1/6:15 precedent. The canon's French 'esclaves' is honestly recorded.

2.80.0 to 2.81.0 minor bump is correct: 12 appliesTo extensions, no wohChoice change. reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line was checked: all 146 lines, and specifically the 21 reception-note sites (7:3, 8:1, 8:7, 8:8, 8:10, 8:12, 9:1, 9:5, 9:9, 9:13, 9:18, 10:4, 10:7, 12:12, 13:18, 16:18, 16:20, 16:21, 21:1, 21:2, 21:3). A script found no Elohim, Yahweh, YHWH, craft, missile, atomic, nuclear, planet, Eternals, loudspeaker or similar lens vocabulary in any line. The only hits were 'ship(s)' (8:9 ploia; worship) and 'Israel' (substring 'rael'), both benign. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own headed paragraph labelled 'reception note, not a translation claim'. Each was verified against LWTE ch. 2 (LWTE-2:155-228), FR and EN. No line resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction: the visionary hōs/homoios markers are kept (8:8; 9:7-10), 'the number of a man' stays open (13:18), 'breastplates' is used rather than the canon's French 'thorax' (9:9), 'pit of the abyss' is kept (9:1), and theos is 'God' where the canon's English has 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' (9:13; 21:2-4). Where the line and the canon's English diverge, the line follows the Greek critical text, and at 8:7 that text agrees with the canon's French.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 146 verses, the 10 overlay entries touched and the 13 diff ops were formed from the chapters, the SBLGNT sources (including the sigla-bearing Rev.txt in the scratchpad), the overlay, the diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-r2-editor-report.md. After reading the report, no verdict changed. The report's Founder point C lists the KJV-wording variants named in commentary (8:7, 9:13, 10:4, 21:2, 21:3 'his people ... their God', 21:4). It omits 21:3 'out of heaven', which confirms the reviewer's 21:3 revise. Its 9:13 request ('the Reviewer should verify this against the NA28 apparatus') was met as far as possible: the SBLGNT marker confirms a collated edition reads tessarōn, and the corrected attribution agrees with the reviewer's reading of Metzger. The printed NA28 apparatus was not available, so this is recorded as unverified at the sigla level, not as a defect. The report's 'All other lines are the Translator's draft, unchanged' was confirmed by diffing against the rev_r2 backup: only 16:3 and 16:9 differ.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-theion-sulfur: Endorse. LXX theion = gophrit (Gen 19:24), BDAG 'sulfur', NRSV 'sulfur' at all four sites; the central entry already renders the Revelation lake passages 'sulfur'. The canon's English 'brimstone' (9:18) is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-theos-God-not-Yahweh-Elohim: Endorse firmly. theos does not render the Tetragrammaton, the canon's own French has 'Dieu', and chapters 1, 4, 6 are signed off with 'God'. Writing 'Yahweh' would translate the canon's English edition, not the Greek.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-critical-text-over-KJV-wording: Endorse. Complete the inventory: add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou) and 16:18 (NA28 singular; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'); correct 8:7 to say the omission is a TR reading, not the Byzantine majority's. Optionally name 16:3 zōsa and 21:4 hoti.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-names-and-scope-rule: Endorse, and support promotion to a central Greek-NT convention. Add the explicit criterion (apply where the central English is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme; background where it imports a Hebrew-specific form), which explains chayyot at 7:11 and gophrit for theion.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-exousia: Endorse. The context rule follows BDAG's sense division and RSV/NRSV practice; 16:9 'authority over' aligns with 6:8 and 13:7. Uniform 'authority' would read badly at 9:10, 19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-16:3-living-being: Endorse. 'soul' for sea creatures imports a personal sense; 'living being' keeps the noun and the nep̄eš ḥayyâ echo.
founderDecisionRecommendations.G-doulos-servants: Endorse. Keeps the signed-off 1:1/6:11 and the canon's English 'servants'; the French 'esclaves' is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.H-pit-of-the-abyss: Endorse. ASV structure; matches the canon's French 'le puits de l'abîme'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.I-Har-magedon: Endorse. ASV form, follows the SBLGNT/NA28 rough breathing, keeps har visible without deciding the etymology.
founderDecisionRecommendations.J-12:18-versification: Endorse. P47, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read estathē, and SBLGNT/NA28 number it 12:18 (Metzger on 12:18). The ASV 13:1a alignment is a tooling task (orchestrator follow-up 2), not a translation issue.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἰσχυρὸν καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, περιβεβλημένον νεφέλην, καὶ ἡ ἶρις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς στῦλοι πυρός,
paragraphs.translit: kai eidon allon angelon ischyron katabainonta ek tou ouranou, peribeblēmenon nephelēn, kai hē iris epi tēn kephalēn autou, kai to prosōpon autou hōs ho hēlios, kai hoi podes autou hōs styloi pyros,

i18n.en: And I saw another mighty angel coming down out of heaven, clothed with a cloud, and the rainbow was upon his head, and his face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire;

notes.official: *allon angelon ischyron* 'another mighty angel', after the mighty angel of 5:2. *peribeblēmenon nephelēn* 'clothed with a cloud': the cloud is the garment and vehicle of theophany (Ps 104:3; Dan 7:13; Rev 1:7). *hē iris* 'the rainbow' has the article, possibly referring back to 4:3. *to prosōpon autou hōs ho hēlios* 'his face was like the sun' recalls 1:16 and the angel of Dan 10:6 (central `angelic-figure-dan-10-5-6-revelation-1-13-15-cross-corpus`, background). *hoi podes autou hōs styloi pyros* 'his feet like pillars of fire': the simile evokes the pillar of fire of the exodus (Ex 13:21-22; central `pillar-of-cloud-and-fire-ammud-ha-anan-ve-esh-divine-presence-marker-cross-corpus`, background, since here it is a comparison). *podes* can also mean 'legs' (BDAG); 'feet' is kept.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ βιβλαρίδιον ἠνεῳγμένον. καὶ ἔθηκεν τὸν πόδα αὐτοῦ τὸν δεξιὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸν δὲ εὐώνυμον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς,
paragraphs.translit: kai echōn en tē cheiri autou biblaridion ēneōgmenon. kai ethēken ton poda autou ton dexion epi tēs thalassēs, ton de euōnymon epi tēs gēs,

i18n.en: and he had in his hand a little book, opened. And he set his right foot upon the sea, and his left upon the earth,

notes.official: *biblaridion ēneōgmenon* 'a little book, opened': *biblaridion* is a diminutive of *biblion* (v 8). A *biblion* is a scroll, and 'book' is kept here as in 'the book of life' (13:8; 21:27); at 6:14 the simile of rolling up required 'scroll'. The opened book recalls the scroll handed to Ezekiel (Ezek 2:9-10). *ethēken ton poda autou ton dexion epi tēs thalassēs* 'he set his right foot upon the sea, and his left upon the earth': a gesture of dominion over the whole world.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὥσπερ λέων μυκᾶται. καὶ ὅτε ἔκραξεν, ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν φωνάς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekraxen phōnē megalē hōsper leōn mykatai. kai hote ekraxen, elalēsan hai hepta brontai tas heautōn phōnas.

i18n.en: and he cried out with a loud voice, as a lion roars. And when he cried out, the seven thunders spoke their own voices.

notes.official: *hōsper leōn mykatai* 'as a lion roars' (*mykaomai* is properly 'low, bellow'): Amos 3:8; Hos 11:10. *elalēsan hai hepta brontai tas heautōn phōnas* 'the seven thunders spoke their own voices': cf. the sevenfold *qôl YHWH* 'voice of YHWH' of Ps 29:3-9, where YHWH's voice is thunder.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, ἤμελλον γράφειν· καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν· Σφράγισον ἃ ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, καὶ μὴ αὐτὰ γράψῃς.
paragraphs.translit: kai hote elalēsan hai hepta brontai, ēmellon graphein· kai ēkousa phōnēn ek tou ouranou legousan· sphragison ha elalēsan hai hepta brontai, kai mē auta grapsēs.

i18n.en: And when the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write; and I heard a voice from heaven saying: "Seal up the things that the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write them."

notes.official:
*ēmellon graphein* 'I was about to write'. *Sphragison ha elalēsan hai hepta brontai, kai mē auta grapsēs* 'Seal up the things that the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write them': the language of Dan 8:26 and 12:4, 9, where Daniel is told to 'shut up the words and seal the book' (central `sealed-book-dan-12-4-9-revelation-jubilees-cross-corpus`). In Daniel the sealing keeps a written revelation for the end; here what is sealed is not written at all, and 22:10 reverses the command for the book as a whole. The Textus Receptus adds *tas phōnas heautōn* 'their voices' after the first *brontai* and *moi* 'to me' after *legousan* (KJV 'had uttered their voices ... saying unto me'). The SBLGNT and NA28 have neither, and the line follows them (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes this verse in the KJV wording and states that what John was told, and asked not to write down, was that there is no God and that those speaking to him were men like himself; this was to remain unwritten until humanity reached a level of technology at which everyone could understand it. The line keeps the Greek 'Seal up' and 'do not write them' and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος, ὃν εἶδον ἑστῶτα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἦρεν τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ τὴν δεξιὰν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν,
paragraphs.translit: kai ho angelos, hon eidon hestōta epi tēs thalassēs kai epi tēs gēs, ēren tēn cheira autou tēn dexian eis ton ouranon,

i18n.en: And the angel whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth lifted up his right hand to heaven,

notes.official: *ēren tēn cheira autou tēn dexian eis ton ouranon* 'lifted up his right hand to heaven': the gesture of oath, from Dan 12:7, where the man clothed in linen lifts both hands to heaven and swears by him who lives for ever (cf. Deut 32:40).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὤμοσεν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ὃς ἔκτισεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ, ὅτι χρόνος οὐκέτι ἔσται·
paragraphs.translit: kai ōmosen tō zōnti eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn, hos ektisen ton ouranon kai ta en autō kai tēn gēn kai ta en autē kai tēn thalassan kai ta en autē, hoti chronos ouketi estai·

i18n.en: and swore by the one who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things in it, and the earth and the things in it, and the sea and the things in it, that there will be delay no longer;

notes.official: *ōmosen ... tō zōnti eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn* 'swore by the one who lives forever and ever' (Dan 12:7). *hos ektisen ton ouranon ... kai tēn gēn ... kai tēn thalassan* 'who created heaven ... and the earth ... and the sea': the threefold creation formula of Ex 20:11 and Neh 9:6. *hoti chronos ouketi estai* 'that there will be delay no longer': *chronos* is time in the sense of 'delay, respite' (BDAG *chronos* 1; cf. 2:21 'I gave her time to repent'; 6:11 'a little while longer'), and the oath answers the martyrs' 'How long?' (6:10). The KJV 'that there should be time no longer' has been read as the end of time itself, but the context, the delay before the seventh trumpet (v 7), supports 'delay' (ASV, RSV, NRSV; Aune, WBC 52B).

paragraphs.text: ἀλλʼ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ ἑβδόμου ἀγγέλου, ὅταν μέλλῃ σαλπίζειν, καὶ ἐτελέσθη τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς εὐηγγέλισεν τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ δούλους τοὺς προφήτας.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ en tais hēmerais tēs phōnēs tou hebdomou angelou, hotan mellē salpizein, kai etelesthē to mystērion tou theou, hōs euēngelisen tous heautou doulous tous prophētas.

i18n.en: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound, then the mystery of God is finished, as he announced as good news to his own servants the prophets.

notes.official:
*all' en tais hēmerais tēs phōnēs tou hebdomou angelou ... kai etelesthē to mystērion tou theou* 'but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel ... then the mystery of God is finished': *kai* introduces the main clause (a Semitic *wə*-apodosis), and the aorist *etelesthē* is proleptic, speaking of a certain future as already done (ASV 'then is finished'; RSV 'the mystery of God ... should be fulfilled'). *mystērion* in apocalyptic is God's hidden plan, now disclosed (Dan 2:28-29, Aramaic *rāz*; 1QpHab 7:4-5). *hōs euēngelisen tous heautou doulous tous prophētas* 'as he announced as good news to his own servants the prophets' echoes Amos 3:7 ('he reveals his secret to his servants the prophets'); 'servants' per `doulos-servant-slave-rendering-revelation`.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes this verse (French 'le mystère de Dieu aussi sera fini comme il en a avisé ses esclaves les prophètes'; English edition 'the mystery of God would be finished') and reads 'the mystery of God' as the understanding, when the time comes, that there is no God and that the Elohim are humanity's creators. The line renders *to mystērion tou theou* literally and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πάλιν λαλοῦσαν μετʼ ἐμοῦ καὶ λέγουσαν· Ὕπαγε λάβε τὸ βιβλίον τὸ ἠνεῳγμένον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ἑστῶτος ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai hē phōnē hēn ēkousa ek tou ouranou, palin lalousan metʼ emou kai legousan· hypage labe to biblion to ēneōgmenon en tē cheiri tou angelou tou hestōtos epi tēs thalassēs kai epi tēs gēs.

i18n.en: And the voice that I had heard from heaven spoke with me again, saying: "Go, take the book that is open in the hand of the angel who is standing upon the sea and upon the earth."

notes.official: *hē phōnē hēn ēkousa ... palin lalousan met' emou kai legousan* 'the voice that I had heard ... spoke with me again, saying': the participles are accusative where a nominative is expected and depend loosely on *ēkousa* 'I heard'; the English supplies a finite verb (ASV 'And the voice which I heard ... I heard it again speaking'). *to biblion to ēneōgmenon* 'the book that is open', the same object as the *biblaridion* of v 2.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθα πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον λέγων αὐτῷ δοῦναί μοι τὸ βιβλαρίδιον. καὶ λέγει μοι· Λάβε καὶ κατάφαγε αὐτό, καὶ πικρανεῖ σου τὴν κοιλίαν, ἀλλʼ ἐν τῷ στόματί σου ἔσται γλυκὺ ὡς μέλι.
paragraphs.translit: kai apēltha pros ton angelon legōn autō dounai moi to biblaridion. kai legei moi· labe kai kataphage auto, kai pikranei sou tēn koilian, allʼ en tō stomati sou estai glyky hōs meli.

i18n.en: And I went to the angel, telling him to give me the little book. And he says to me: "Take it and eat it up; and it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey."

notes.official: *legōn autō dounai moi* 'telling him to give me'. *Labe kai kataphage auto* 'Take it and eat it up': Ezek 2:8-3:3, where the scroll is 'as honey for sweetness' in the prophet's mouth. The bitterness in the stomach is John's addition: the message is sweet to receive and bitter in its content. *koilia* 'stomach' (ASV 'belly').

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ βιβλαρίδιον ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου καὶ κατέφαγον αὐτό, καὶ ἦν ἐν τῷ στόματί μου ὡς μέλι γλυκύ· καὶ ὅτε ἔφαγον αὐτό, ἐπικράνθη ἡ κοιλία μου.
paragraphs.translit: kai elabon to biblaridion ek tēs cheiros tou angelou kai katephagon auto, kai ēn en tō stomati mou hōs meli glyky· kai hote ephagon auto, epikranthē hē koilia mou.

i18n.en: And I took the little book out of the hand of the angel and ate it up, and it was in my mouth sweet as honey; and when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.

notes.official: The fulfilment repeats v 9 in reverse order, mouth first and then stomach. *epikranthē hē koilia mou* 'my stomach was made bitter'.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ λέγουσίν μοι· Δεῖ σε πάλιν προφητεῦσαι ἐπὶ λαοῖς καὶ ἔθνεσιν καὶ γλώσσαις καὶ βασιλεῦσιν πολλοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai legousin moi· dei se palin prophēteusai epi laois kai ethnesin kai glōssais kai basileusin pollois.

i18n.en: And they say to me: "You must prophesy again over many peoples and nations and tongues and kings."

notes.official: *legousin moi* 'they say to me': an indefinite plural equivalent to a passive ('I was told'). *prophēteusai epi laois kai ethnesin* 'prophesy over many peoples and nations': *epi* with the dative can mean 'about, concerning' (RSV, NRSV; BDAG *epi* 8), 'against' (cf. Ezek 4:7 LXX) or 'over'. The ASV 'over' is kept because it leaves that range open; cf. Jer 1:10, the prophet set 'over the nations and over the kingdoms'.
